title: Deterministic kernel scoring and attention micro-batching action plan
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Summary: Following an increase in p95/p99 latencies across customer workloads after the scheduler's recent heuristic changes (Feb 14 rollout), we observed nondeterministic kernel reroutes driven by aggressive probe scoring. This ticket contains a concrete, minimum-risk plan to: 1) replace the current probabilistic probe scoring with a deterministic, explainable kernel ranking; 2) introduce attention micro-batching to avoid attention-split oscillation on mid-length requests; and 3) add hysteresis and soft-fallback smoothing in the scheduler to prevent flip-flop reroutes. Goal: reduce tail latency by 30-50% for affected flows without materially increasing average per-token cost.
postmortem_summary: Root cause: probe-driven ranking amplified transient signals (short-lived KV-cache misses, transient memory pressure) that made the scheduler prefer suboptimal fused-attn/quant kernels for bursts. Change set that introduced heuristic tuning removed a small randomness buffer that used to soften transitions. Consequence: bursts saw kernel flip-flop across batches leading to cache churn and increased p99. Contributing factors: lack of hysteresis in ranking score, insufficient telemetry on probe frequency, and no canary that captured long-tail heavy-concurrency traces.
updates: 2026-02-18: Initial triage by oncall; revert candidate change flagged but not rolled back to avoid destabilizing other tenants.
2026-02-20: Collected repro traces from customers A & B; built synthetic stress harness reproducing path oscillation at 250-600 concurrent requests.

2026-02-23: Prototype of deterministic kernel scoring implemented (score features: fused-availability, quant-compat, seq-len-match, kv-cache-hit-rate, probe-penalty). Benchmarked on small fleet; baseline p95 improved ~22% on repro.
2026-03-01: Implemented micro-batching for attention split in runtime (configurable window=10ms/4 requests); increased CPU by ~3% but reduced p99 for mid-length sequences.
2026-03-05: Scheduler hysteresis strategy added: exponential decay of probe penalty with configurable half-life; prevents immediate re-selection for N seconds after route change.
2026-03-09: QA and perf team ran canary across test cluster; observed one regression in throughput for a small subset of long-sequence streaming tests.
2026-03-10: Product/SDR review — agreed canary rollout plan (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with rollback gates on p95, throughput, and error-rate thresholds.
2026-03-12: Merged deterministic scoring and hysteresis to staging; micro-batching flag gated off by default pending canary.
Next steps: run 48h canary at 5% on lower-impact customers, add new dashboards for probe-rate and kernel-switch-counts, follow up on throughput regression root cause.
